correctness.rationale: For every A≥B>0, K={|x|/A+|y|/B≤1}, any inscribed rectangle can be centered without changing its area by averaging with its reflection. Centered rectangles correspond to equal-length diagonals v,w and area 2|det(v,w)|. At an optimizer either both tips lie on the boundary or the variable interior tip has a perpendicular diagonal by first variation. In perpendicular branch concavity of (sinθ/A+cosθ/B) on 0≤θ≤π/4 reduces extremum to endpoints, bounding det by max(B²,AB/2); in boundary branch equal-norm quadratic yields s=t or s+t=2A²/(A²+B²), both with determinant bound max(AB/2,B²). Midpoint rectangle area AB and diagonal square area 2B² attain sharp max; equality cases and side contacts rule out translations and extra optima, including the B/A=1/2 tie and A=B. Independently checked boundary identity algebra and 240,000 random feasible centered rectangles; finite experiments not an exhaustive geometry proof.
